title: Practice 2: вз- (вс-): up — на-: onto, and a quantity covered

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Закройте окна, а то комары ___ (налететь / налетать).
exercises.why: **налетят** is the future tense (3rd person plural) of **налететь** (to fly (upon, against), to come flying (to); (colloquial) to bump (into), to run (into), to hit, to collide (with)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **налетать**. future: я налечу́ · ты налети́шь · он налети́т · мы налети́м · вы налети́те · они налетя́т. — Wiktionary, «налететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. Prepositional phrases: в/на + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Close the windows. Otherwise, mosquitoes will get in.
exercises.context: **на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Prepositional phrases: в/на + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Tom is tidying up his room.
exercises.context: **на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Мэри ___ (нанести / наносить) на лицо увлажняющий крем.
exercises.why: **нанесла** is the past tense (feminine) of **нанести** (to drift (on); to carry, to waft, to deposit, to wash ashore (e.g. of snow, sand, etc.)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **наносить**. past: он нанёс · она нанесла́ · оно нанесло́ · они нанесли́. — Wiktionary, «нанести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. Prepositional phrases: в/на + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Mary applied moisturizing cream to her face.
exercises.context: **на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: One king after another succeeded to the throne during those few years.
exercises.why: **всходил** is the past tense (masculine) of **всходить** (to mount, to go up, to climb, to ascend; (of a heavenly body) to rise) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **взойти**. past: он всходи́л · она всходи́ла · оно всходи́ло · они всходи́ли. — Wiktionary, «всходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вз-, взо-, воз-, вс-, вос-** — Movement upwards. Antonym: с- Example: Альпинист взошёл на гору. — The mountain climber walked up the mountain. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **сходил** (**сходить**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.ru: В эти несколько лет один король ___ на престол за другим.
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: с- Example: Альпинист взошёл на гору. — The mountain climber walked up the mountain. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
